t: The pot is too full to stir and too empty to feed everyone.
I need to soak the grain earlier tomorrow.
Everyone likes supper until it is their turn to clean the pot.
The roots are sweet today. That saves me from hearing complaints.
I can smell when the fire is too hot before I see it.
A little salt would rescue this whole meal.
I put aside a bowl for whoever comes in late.
The children know exactly when I start serving.
I should sharpen the small knife. It crushes more than it cuts.
Hot food makes a hard day easier to forgive.
The map looks certain where my feet remember mud.
I should have marked that fork before walking past it.
Every ridge promises a shorter route and usually lies.
I found good water today. That makes the whole walk useful.
My boots know this country better than the map does.
The road home always looks clearer than the road out.
I need more cord for marking trees.
That valley deserves another look when the weather clears.
I was certain the village lay west. It did not.
A useful journey is mostly noticing what everyone else walked past.
The soil breaks better after rain, but my back does not.
I can tell which rows I rushed by looking from here.
The birds wait until I turn around. They know the work.
I should save more seed than feels necessary.
One healthy shoot makes the empty patches easier to bear.
The weeds grow wherever my hands are not.
I watered that corner twice and it still looks offended.
Straight rows please me more than they should.
Harvest always feels far away until it arrives all at once.
Tomorrow I start with the row I avoided today.
Most of guarding is noticing the same quiet things again.
I should oil the spear shaft before the wood splits.
That shadow is a bush. It was also a bush yesterday.
I would rather be bored all night than surprised once.
The outer path needs another torch before winter.
People sleep better when they see someone standing watch.
My feet hurt more from standing than they ever did from walking.
I counted every house twice. Everyone is inside.
A loose gate makes every sound feel important.
Dawn is close. I can feel myself becoming less patient.
That bandage will hold if they stop touching it.
I need more clean water before the next dressing.
People remember pain clearly and instructions poorly.
The fever broke before dawn. I can breathe easier now.
I can stitch skin. I cannot stitch patience into the person wearing it.
The bruise looks worse today, which sometimes means it is healing.
I should check the old wound before they start work.
Clean cloth disappears faster than food around here.
I know when somebody is pretending not to limp.
A quiet patient worries me more than a complaining one.
The rock sounded hollow behind that face.
Dust finds its way through every fold of cloth.
I should replace the wedge before it breaks inside the crack.
Good stone separates cleanly. This stone wants an argument.
The lamp looked dim long before I admitted it.
Every load feels heavier once daylight is visible.
I found a dark seam today. I need better light before following it.
The supports held, but I heard them complain.
Stone chips have worked into both boots again.
I keep striking the same place because eventually the rock must lose.
That joint fits cleanly. I will notice it every time I pass.
I need a longer straightedge before the next wall.
The doorway looked wide until we moved the table through it.
A good roof hides how many arguments built it.
I should save those offcuts. Small wood solves large problems.
I should speak less at the shrine and listen longer afterward.
People bring practical troubles and expect sacred answers.
The same prayer sounds different from a full stomach.
I need to remember who came alone today.
Certainty is easy from the front of a crowd.
